title: Excel on the web: Copilot Agent Mode (Edit with Copilot) builds and edits workbooks through chat
summary: Hold: Copilot could already write into Excel workbooks before this change, contrary to the briefing's claim that it previously only suggested changes. The roadmap facts, licence requirement and printed control commands are supported; the Anthropic defaults and provider-wide scope need qualifications from Microsoft's regional documentation.

claims.claim: Before this change, Copilot only suggested changes rather than writing into the workbook.

The March 10, 2026 release notes at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes support this narrower description.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center licence control is at Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with the printed UserId, AddLicenses SkuId and empty RemoveLicenses assigns the selected licence.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center route reaches the Anthropic user and group access control.
claims.quote: Copilot > Settings > View all. ... AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors ... under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic ... Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences, select your users or groups

claims.claim: No automation for the Anthropic subprocessor access setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Anthropic AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors Microsoft Graph API PowerShell setting'; 'Anthropic Graph subprocessor API'. Opened connect-to-ai-subprocessor, copilotPolicySetting and configure-copilot-admin-center; no provider-setting API found.

claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the Copilot DLP location used to exclude labelled workbooks.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. ... On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: The path reaches the policy location but stops before the label-processing control. Append ' > rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels > Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content' to controls[2].ui.path and its rendered table entry, using the condition and action documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about.

claims.claim: The printed New-DLPComplianceRule command creates the rule excluding labelled content from Copilot processing.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: DLP sensitivity-label exclusion covers Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork and Copilot in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
claims.quote: This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: Copilot skills are disabled when a workbook with a label excluded by DLP is open in Excel.
claims.quote: When a file is open in Word, Excel, or PowerPoint and has a sensitivity label for which DLP policy is configured to prevent processing by Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat, the skills in these apps are disabled.
claims.fix: Add Microsoft's qualification: 'Certain experiences that do not reference file content or do not use large language models are not currently blocked in the user experience.' The surrounding note at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about states this exception.

claims.claim: The content-processing DLP policy is evaluated at file open in Excel.
claims.quote: In Word, Excel, and PowerPoint the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy to prevent Copilot from processing content is evaluated at file open.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label applied mid-session is enforced the next time the file is opened.
claims.quote: If a sensitivity label is applied mid-session, the policy will be enforced starting the next time the file is opened.

claims.claim: The DLP rule condition is Content contains > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: | Content contains > Sensitivity labels | Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content |

claims.claim: The DLP action is Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content.
claims.quote: | Content contains > Sensitivity labels | Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content |

claims.claim: No tenant UI or API switch specifically turning Edit with Copilot in Excel on or off on its own is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Excel Edit with Copilot policy disable'; 'Excel Agent Mode admin disable'. Opened release notes, configure-copilot-admin-center and copilotPolicySetting; found general controls, but no separate Excel Edit with Copilot switch.

claims.claim: No change to sign-in or permissions is documented for this roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edit with Copilot sign-in permissions'; 'Edit with Copilot Excel Agent Mode disable admin policy setting sign in permissions audit events'. Read the roadmap, release notes and Business Central Excel guidance; no item-specific sign-in or permission change found.

claims.claim: The copilotPolicySetting reference lists Block Copilot Access to Open Content.
claims.quote: | microsoft.copilot.blockaccesstoopenfiles | Block Copilot Access to Open Content |

claims.claim: Which audit events distinguish Edit with Copilot workbook changes from the user's own edits remains an open question.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edit with Copilot Excel Agent Mode disable admin policy setting sign in permissions audit events'. Read audit-copilot and audit-log-activities search excerpts; they document Excel interactions and CopilotInteraction, not distinct workbook-edit events.
